span.label: RETRACTED (TWO EFFECTS OF A COMMON CAUSE, TAGGED AS CAUSING EACH OTHER - a class I have not named before) · hippocampus —causes→ behavioral performance
span.note: RETRACTED: TWO EFFECTS OF A COMMON CAUSE, TAGGED AS CAUSING EACH OTHER - a class I have not named before. The edge is `hippocampus --causes--> behavioral performance`. The span is a chain of PREDICTIONS: 'we PREDICTED that subjects who could not maintain a sustained focus of attention ... would rely more on LTM, and, THEREFORE, Quotation withheld. These subjects, however, WOULD PERFORM POORLY on the task BECAUSE recalling the tone from LTM would entail proactive interference'. The upstream cause is failure to sustain attention, which produces LTM reliance; LTM reliance produces BOTH greater hippocampal activation AND poor performance. Hippocampal activation is a MARKER of the same upstream process, not a cause of the performance. Reading the two consequences as one causing the other is the classic confound, and here the paper itself lays the structure out. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): housed below as the common-cause structure, since no type can record 'these two share a cause'. — strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — SIGN NEGATIVE, AND PREDICTED IN ADVANCE FROM THE RIVAL'S MODEL: more hippocampal activity should mean worse performance if it reflects falling back on long-term memory
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: DMN —causes→ behavioral performance
span.note: status: CORRELATIONAL, NOT INTERVENTIONAL: the paper reports a negative CORRELATION between DMN activity and performance; nothing was manipulated, and the mind-wandering account that follows is offered as an interpretation · direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.7 — SIGN NEGATIVE: read as mind wandering during the delay

span.note: status: CORRELATIONAL: `NEGATIVE CORRELATION was also observed in the right IFJ`. The cited name is the subject of a result verb and the sentence carries no first-person marker, so the finding, quantity or definition is the CITED author's rather than this record's. The claim is true and the quote is verbatim - what is wrong is whose result the corpus says it is. Nothing edited, nothing withdrawn: the row is marked so a page can name the source.
